harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across the cluster: node1 (10.100.99.10) as the writable primary, node2 and node3 as async read-only standbys built via pg_basebackup with a dedicated replicator role. Verified writes on node1 replicate to both standbys and standbys reject writes. Completed the mandatory sequential restart protocol (node2, node3, node1) with boot-id proof of each reboot and post-restart verification of PostgreSQL activity, recovery/streaming state, and data integrity (including a post-restart write/read round trip).
actions_performed: Inspected all three nodes (RHEL 10, no PostgreSQL pre-installed)
Installed postgresql-server/postgresql-contrib 16.14 on node1, node2, node3 (retried node2 after transient GPG fetch error)

Initialized DB on node1 and configured postgresql.conf (listen_addresses, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, max_replication_slots, hot_standby) and pg_hba.conf for replication/app connections from the cluster subnet
Started postgresql on node1 and created a 'replicator' role with a randomly generated password (kept out of command text via secret_env)
Opened firewalld postgresql service on node1 (was blocking pg_basebackup with 'No route to host')
Ran pg_basebackup -R from node1 on node2 and node3 to clone the primary and auto-generate standby.signal/primary_conninfo
Started postgresql on node2 and node3, confirmed streaming state on primary and pg_is_in_recovery=true on standbys
Created repl_test table on primary, inserted a row, confirmed it appeared on both standbys, and confirmed standbys reject INSERTs (read-only)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on all three nodes
Sequentially rebooted node2, then node3, then node1 (primary last) via systemctl reboot backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled each node until reachable again and proved boot_id changed after each reboot
Verified postgresql active and recovery/streaming state restored, and repl_test data intact after each node's restart
Performed a final post-restart write on primary and confirmed it replicated to both standbys

evidence.summary: postgresql-server 16.14 installed successfully on node1, node2 (after retry), and node3
initdb run, postgresql.conf/pg_hba.conf updated for streaming replication, service started, replicator role created

evidence.requirement: Standbys built from primary and configured read-only
evidence.summary: firewall opened, pg_basebackup -R succeeded on node2 and node3 producing standby.signal + primary_conninfo, postgresql started on both

evidence.requirement: Streaming replication established and standbys read-only
evidence.summary: pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both standbys in 'streaming' state; pg_is_in_recovery() true on node2/node3

evidence.requirement: Changes on primary visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 appears on node2 and node3; both standbys reject INSERT as read-only transactions

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6d37896c..., reboot acked, unreachable then boot_id changed to a36b4a70..., postgresql active + in recovery + repl_test data present, primary shows node2 streaming again

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e625b9a5..., reboot acked, unreachable then boot_id changed to 3a26b4cd..., postgresql active + in recovery + repl_test data present, primary shows both standbys streaming

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 180a78a0..., reboot acked, unreachable then boot_id changed to fd2965a8..., postgresql active with repl_test data intact and both standbys reconnected/streaming
New row inserted on primary after all restarts appears on both standbys, confirming replication fully functional post-restart
